children.label: Section heading
children.text: Two decades of Iberian-lexified creole scholarship

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: ACBLPE is a scientific association dedicated to the study of Iberian-lexified creole languages and their communities, and more generally linguistic contact involving Portuguese or Spanish.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Since 2001 its annual meetings have been held in Europe, Africa, the Caribbean and South America, alternating where possible between the Iberian Peninsula and other parts of the world.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: The 25ᵗʰ Conference extends this trajectory to South Asia, bringing creolists into dialogue with researchers of the Indian Ocean’s linguistic and historical contexts.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: The Satellite Conference will showcase research in contact linguistics involving the languages of South Asia and provide a platform for discussing diverse linguistic contact situations in the region. It aims to bring together renowned scholars and researchers in linguistics and to encourage dialogue on the processes, outcomes, and dynamics of language contact in South Asia.

children.label: Page heading
children.text: A small state with a proud history

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Konkani is Goa’s official language; Marathi, Hindi and English are widely spoken, and Portuguese survives in older families and place names.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: The conference falls at the tail of the monsoon. Expect warm, humid days around 28–30°C, occasional showers and a countryside at its greenest.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: 451 years of Portuguese rule left Goa a blend of Indian and Iberian worlds — baroque churches, whitewashed chapels, azulejo tiles and Indo-Portuguese mansions.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Fish curry rice, xacuti, sorpotel, vindaloo and bebinca. Vegetarian thalis and international cuisine are easy to find everywhere.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Panjim’s Latin Quarter, five minutes from the university — colour-washed Portuguese houses, chapels and bakeries.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Bom Jesus Basilica, Se Cathedral and St. Augustine ruins, a UNESCO World Heritage ensemble about 30 km away.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Evening cruises from the Panjim jetty with Goan music and dance, a short ride from campus.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Ferry crossings, village lanes and the Dr. Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary — at their most beautiful just after the rains.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: One of India’s tallest waterfalls, at full force in early September, on the Karnataka border.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: A guided walk through a working spice farm with a traditional Goan lunch, about 30 km inland.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Miramar and Dona Paula are minutes from campus; Calangute and Baga lie further north.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Try local cafés and family kitchens for vindaloo, chorizo pão and bebinca dessert.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Fort Aguada and Chapora above the mouths of the Mandovi and Chapora rivers.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Museum of Goa in Pilerne and the Goa State Museum, both a short drive away.

pages.name: Call for Papers
pages.title: Call for Papers | ACBLPE 2027
pages.description: Call for papers for the ACBLPE 2027 conference.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Abstracts are invited on any topic of language contact involving Portuguese or Spanish. Submissions open 30 October 2026 and close 15 January 2027.

children.label: Link
children.note: Destination: https://easyabs.linguistlist.org/; opens in a new tab.

children.label: Decorative image
children.note: Alt text is empty for decorative imagery.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Use these nine points as a checklist for a clear, well-supported abstract.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Many abstracts are rejected because they omit crucial information rather than because of errors in what they include. A suggested outline for abstracts follows:

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Choose a title that clearly indicates the topic of the paper and is no more than one line long.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: In the abstract, state the topic clearly.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Make reference to prior work on the topic.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: When essential to the clarity of the argumentation, present linguistic data (with glosses).

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Explain abbreviations at their first occurrence.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: If the paper presents the results of experiments but the collection of results is not yet complete, present the provisional results in detail. Also indicate the nature of the experimental design and the specific hypothesis tested.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: State the relevance of your hypothesis to past work. Describe the analysis in as much detail as possible. Avoid vague or unsubstantiated statements.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: State the contribution to linguistic research made by the analysis.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Citation of the relevant literature is essential within the abstract; however, the inclusion of a list of references at the end of the abstract is not obligatory.

children.label: Section heading
children.text: Clarity in research. Dialogue in presentation.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Reviewer instructions: abstracts will be assessed based on the following three criteria:

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: The relevance and significance of the proposed topic and/or the originality of the study.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: The argumentation (including the clarity of the argument and the results/conclusions).

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Knowledge of the relevant research literature and theory.

children.label: Paragraph
children.text: Abstracts may be submitted in Creole, English, French, Portuguese or Spanish. Presentations should be delivered in the same language as the abstract, although the screen language and spoken language may differ.
